entry.title: Show HN: Productivity FOSS App Synced in Desktop and Mobile (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: Some of the many things it offers: Plan: your week with time blocks, repeating or one-off. You can skip or move a single occurrence and save week templates. External calendars show next to it, and there's an ICS feed out. Board / Todos: today as a kanban board, plus undated todos with tags, filters, attributes and links. Putting a todo on a day schedules it. Weekly review: clear out stale todos and write a note on the week. Notebooks: notes per subject in folders, a diary, ideas, people (birthdays, relationships, every mention of them). Those work as scopes, they can hold everything mentioned here: goals, workouts, inventory, tasks, etc. Goals: numeric targets and progress logs. You can link tasks to a goal, so finishing them moves it. Health: habit tracking with a heatmap, and workouts that log reps, kg and km per exercise. You can put those on a date too, log how much weight you lifted, the distance you ran, etc. Inventory / Shopping: things you own with quantities and restocking. Recipes use inventory items as ingredients, and what's missing goes to the shopping list, which you can open offline in the market to see what is missing. Finance: ledgers, statement import, auto-sorting rules, bills. Also integrates with inventory prices. Media: a gallery and audio recordings. You can put those on notes and tasks, or standalone. Reminders: on blocks and todos. You get notifications on the mobile app or PC. A quick add (+) wheel menu for adding any important thing with one finger movement. Everything can have tags, many things can have attributes (key value pairs) that can be used with integrations: it comes with a REST API and a MCP server; you can use any AI to talk to it through scoped tokens that allow you to keep your privacy from AI companies by only giving it access to one particular project (Notebook) and its goals, tasks, notes, inventory items etc. It's keyboard-driven (vim-style keys) too, and you can run it in the phone both in sync with the official / you self-hosted instance, or fully isolated (never sees the internet). entry.title: Tell HN: Uceprotect is extorting website owners (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: I recently discovered by accident that our website was being blocked by Orange's security filters. After a quick check, I found that our IP address is listed on UCEPROTECT Level 3. The listing is based on the reputation of the entire ASN 14061 (DigitalOcean, US) [1]. In other words, even if your IP did nothing wrong, it will still be listed because of its ASN. If your site is innocent and listed only because it's hosted on DigitalOcean, UCEPROTECT offers to whitelist it for about $30/month or $108/year [2]. I checked the ASNs of several other popular hosting providers, and they're all listed too. So if your site is hosted on DigitalOcean or any other major provider, it's probably blacklisted as well. That can cut you off from customers on mobile networks like Orange, whose "cybersecurity protection" uses blacklists like UCEPROTECT to filter traffic. Honestly, in my 20-year career, this is the first time I've seen a blacklist misbehave this badly and ask for money when there's clearly been no wrongdoing. [1] http://www.uceprotect.net/en/rblcheck.php?asn=14061 [2] https://www.whitelisted.org/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49964045 Points: 69 # Comments: 29
